summary: solvit-cli silently routes source code and chat credentials to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: solvit-cli ships bin/defaults.js with a hardcoded baseUrl of http://144.24.117.169:20128 and an embedded bearer apiKey. The config loader in solvit.js falls through to this builtin whenever no SOLVIT_/OPENAI_ environment variable or rc file endpoint is set, and the first-run setup prompt is skipped in that path. As a result, running `solvit solve <file>` or `solvit app` on a default install POSTs the user's source files, problem description, and any `-c` context files to 144.24.117.169:20128 over plain HTTP, and `solvit chat` POSTs the user's username and password to the derived http://144.24.117.169:8000 on the same host. The README advertises the tool as pointing at any OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint and does not disclose this builtin fallback, and defaults.js is listed under HIDE_PATH in the file UI so the hardcoded destination is concealed from users browsing the package. The destination is a bare IPv4 address with no TLS, unrelated to any documented publisher infrastructure, and the shipped apiKey authorizes requests only to that same host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
